Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the Bangladesh Women. Out walk the two openers for South Africa Women, Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits. Marufa Akter will start with the new ball for Bangladesh Women. A slip in place. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

South Africa Women knew that the wicket was going to be slow and tried their best to pick up early wickets which wasn't the case. Marizanne Kapp toiled hard but did pick up a wicket in her comeback spell and eventually ended up with two to her name. Kapp also achieved the unique feat of taking 150 plus wickets and scoring 2500 plus runs in Women's ODI, a feat achieved only by two other players before her. The rest of the bowling was decent but Eliz-Mari Marx did leak a few runs. The target isn't a big one but given the nature of the pitch, Bangladesh Women's spinners will come into play. South Africa Women will also have the last game on their mind which could make things even more interesting. Join us in a bit for the run chase.

Marizanne Kapp is down for a quick chat. She says she is extremely happy to take her 150th wicket. She is a bit disappointed as the bowling was not on point from their side, and which allowed the visitors to score more runs, but she has full faith in her batting lineup to chase the target on the board.

Bangladesh Women started the second match just like they started the first game, with a solid foundation up top. The pair of Shamima Sultana and Fargana Hoque started watchfully but ensured their side didn't lose early wickets. Shamima looked like the aggressor and looked in flow as well but got out in the twenties. Hoque took up the mantle and stitched together a couple of decent stands. She continued to press and found a solid partner in the form of Fahima Khatun at the other end after the loss of three wickets. Hoque went on to score her second ODI ton, which made her the only Bangladesh Women batter to achieve that feat but unfortunately, she couldn't remain unbeaten. Khatun though finished well and ended unbeaten on 46 runs.

End of an engrossing first innings and the game seems to be evenly poised at the halfway mark. Bangladesh Women would have wanted to get a few more runs but will take 222 runs given what happened in the last game and South Africa Women will be happy to restrict the opposition to a chasable total.

South Africa Women on the other hand weren't at their best with either bat or ball as has been the case throughout this tour. They failed to pick wickets in a bunch and allowed their opponents to put on a big total on the board and then simply crumbled with the bat. Former skipper Sune Luus and Eliz-Mari Marx were the only batters to put some runs on the board and get into the thirties but overall, they were well below their best. Can the hosts come back and get back on level terms? Or will Bangladesh Women pick up a memorable series win away from home? We shall find out in due course. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Bangladesh Women put 250 runs on the board thanks to a very well-rounded batting performance from the top five batters but one name stood out and that was Murshida Khatun who made 91 big runs. With the ball, they were on the money as well, bowling as a group and everyone contributed with Nahida Akter ending up with three wickets. Nigar Sultana will look to rally her troops to a big away series win here.

The visitors have a 1-0 lead in the three-game series and will look to win the series in this game. The hosts on the other hand need to step up quickly if they are to level the series and make the final game an interesting one.

The action moves from East London to Potchefstroom as high-flying Bangladesh Women aim to seal the deal in the second ODI of the series. It was a historic performance from the Bangladesh unit in the first match where they outclassed South Africa Women by a handsome margin and registered their biggest win by runs in this format. It also happened to be their first win over the home team since 2017 and what a way it was to end that drought. Bangladesh Women have punched above their weight on this tour and continue to showcase their growth. The pitch at Buffalo Park aided the gameplan of Bangladesh Women and they played on their strength. Their main batter took the responsibilities and showed great form, and once there was a good total on the board, the Bangla spinners got into the act. The visitors will be hoping for more of the same in the upcoming game to gain an unassailable lead in the series. South Africa Women, on the other hand, will be crestfallen after suffering such a hefty defeat. They will be looking to leave that behind immediately and come up with a kind of performance that the cricketing world usually associates with them. Their bowling in the last game wasn't up to the mark and to compound their misery, the collapse during the chase badly exposed their batting depth. The hosts will have to display a lot of character to bounce back and if they do that, we will be in for a cracking contest.
